My name is enough — I am an old man now, 56 years, and I have been farming this land in Tabora since I was a boy. This plot of mine is more than six hectares, but I plant it mixed — you know, when you intercrop, the crops help each other and if one fails the other gives you something to eat. I do not have money for chemical fertilizer this season, and the dukas in town are charging too much for urea. I will use the cattle manure we collect at the boma, plant the seed I saved from last year, and rely on my family to do most of the work. For weeding when the rains come strong, I will call two or three young men from the village to help me, because at my age I cannot bend in the field all day.
